title: 3.2.26 Lab: findMax & isEven
description: Define two functions, findMax(a, b) and isEven(n), that take parameters and return a value. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define findMax
steps.instructions: Define a function called findMax that takes two parameters, a and b. Inside the function, compare a and b, then return whichever value is larger.

steps.title: Define isEven
steps.instructions: Define a function called isEven that takes one parameter, n. Inside the function, use the remainder operator % to check whether n is even, and return true or false.

steps.title: Call both functions
steps.instructions: Call findMax and isEven with sample values and log the results with console.log to verify your functions work.

requirements.description: findMax(a, b) gives back whichever of the two numbers is larger, whichever order they come in. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: findMax must hand back the LARGER of a and b. Check which way your comparison points, and that both branches return a value.

requirements.description: isEven(n) returns true when n is even and false when it is odd, including 0 and negative numbers. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: isEven must return true or false (not 0 or 1): an even number has a remainder of 0 when divided by 2.
